name: namht-spec-ui
description: Point-and-click UI over the namht-* namht Kit skills for non-technical roles (PM/SM). Runs Claude Code under the hood.

namhtSpecUi.claudePath.description: Path to the Claude Code CLI executable. (machine-scoped: a workspace cannot override which binary is launched).

namhtSpecUi.extraArgs.description: Extra args passed to `claude -p`. Default `bypassPermissions` lets skills run the tools they need headlessly (node for the map/PDF, npm/npx/jest for build & tests, gh, curl) — otherwise those Bash commands fail, because a headless run cannot answer an approval prompt. TRADE-OFF: this mode also permits any Bash command, writes outside the workspace, reading files such as .env, and network calls; Anthropic recommends it only in an isolated environment. The git-guard PreToolUse hook still blocks dangerous/remote git in this mode (hooks run before the permission check - verified), but it is defense-in-depth, not a sandbox. Prefer prompts? Set ["--permission-mode","acceptEdits"] - then map/build/test commands fail in this panel; use the Interactive button (a real terminal) for those instead.

namhtSpecUi.usdToVnd.description: Approx VND per USD, shown next to the USD cost. Adjust to your rate; set 0 to hide VND.

namhtSpecUi.model.description: DEFAULT model pre-selected in each form's Model dropdown (passed as `claude --model`). You can override it per run and per follow-up in the panel. 'sonnet' is ~5x cheaper than Opus for read-only Q&A/planning at great quality; 'haiku' is cheapest for simple lookups; 'opus' for the hardest code tasks; empty = your Claude default.

enumDescriptions: Every skill, including the seven that change code.
Only skills that never touch your source — for PM/SM. The code-editing cards are hidden and the host refuses them even if requested.
namhtSpecUi.mode.description: Which skills this panel offers. 'readonly' hides the seven code-editing skills (build, fix-bug, migrate, simplify, perf, observe, rails-to-spring) and blocks them in the extension host — use it for the .vsix you hand to non-developers.

enumDescriptions: Tiếng Việt — for a Vietnamese-speaking PM/SM.
namhtSpecUi.language.description: Language for the panel's own labels and buttons. It does NOT change the language Claude answers in — that comes from the skill and from how you write the request.
